Aukstadvaris Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vilniaus apskritis, Lithuania

Not demolished. Aukstadvaris, known in the 19th century as Vysokiy Dvor or Wysoki Dwor, had Jews settled before the 17th century; the community grew to 309 people (43.5 percent) by 1897, drawing its cultural, educational, and economic life largely from Vilnius, 40 miles away, including Haskalah and Zionist activity, though the town retained its own synagogue. Two Jews were elected to the local council during the interwar period. Before the 1941 German occupation, the community numbered 230; locals murdered five Jews immediately after the invasion, and the rest were put to forced labor. On September 22, 1941, Rosh Hashanah, Aukstadvaris's Jews were brought to Trakai, and on September 30, the eve of Yom Kippur, they were executed by local Lithuanian police. Eight Jews survived in the forests.
